generation.text: A common weather pattern is a thunderstorm. The reason for the occurrence of a thunderstorm is due to the collision of warm and cool air. When warm, moist air rises up through cool air, it cools and condenses into clouds. As more warm air keeps rising, it forms larger and denser clouds. The water droplets in these clouds collide and stick together, getting bigger and heavier until they become too heavy and fall as rain. The rapid up and down movement of air in these clouds also generates static electricity, and when the electricity becomes strong enough, it discharges as lightning. This is why we often see lightning before we hear thunder - the lightning travels much faster than the sound waves of thunder.
